sections.h2: Where does an Isabella County deed get filed?
sections.html:
Filing happens in Room 220 of the county building at 200 N. Main Street, Mount Pleasant, MI 48858. The office phone is (989) 317-4089. The office keeps land records that reach back to the mid-1800s, and once a document is recorded anyone may review or copy it. Staff neither draft documents nor answer legal questions, so a lawyer or closing company should finish the paperwork first.

The county seat and biggest city is Mount Pleasant. Territorial lawmakers described the county in 1831, it was organized in 1859, and its name honors Queen Isabella I of Castile. When your Isabella County house sells, the closing deed lands at this counter, and the county urges a careful read against the recording rules before anything is handed in.

sections.h2: What do Isabella County statutes set as the filing charge?
sections.html:
State law sets a flat $30.00 for each document. If a document lists several liber and page references, each one beyond the first costs $3.00. Mail-in filers who want the original back should send a prepaid return envelope.

sections.h2: Which sales in Isabella County need a tax certificate first?
sections.html:
Section 211.135 of Michigan law requires a treasurer certificate before the office will file any of these:

  • A warranty deed.
  • Any deed that contains a covenant of warranty.
  • A land contract.
  • An assignment of a land contract with a warranty clause.
  • A master deed for a condominium.

The treasurer issues it, so the check goes to the Isabella County Treasurer. Parcels with many descriptions pay 20 cents for each one after the fifth. Have your closing agent request the certificate before signing day so it cannot delay the filing.

sections.h2: What recording rules do Isabella County deeds have to meet?
sections.html:
The county posts a summary of the Michigan recording rules people ask about most, and refers readers to the legislature's website for the full text. Highlights from that list:

  • Signatures are original, with the names typed, stamped or printed beneath them, and names must agree among the body, signature and acknowledgment.
  • The addresses of all parties appear on an instrument that conveys, assigns or encumbers title.
  • A Michigan-signed deed carries a notary acknowledgment and the name and address of the person who drafted it.
  • When a conveyance names a survivor in the grantor's section, a certified death certificate is recorded as its own document.
  • A trust agreement that accompanies an instrument is recorded separately, under Public Act 194 of 2018.
  • Court orders are certified and sealed by the court clerk.
  • Page one leaves 2 1/2 inches blank at the top, other margins run 1/2 inch, and the type is black, 10 point or larger, on white paper.
  • A foreign-language document comes with a written English translation.

A county news item says Public Acts 191 through 200 of 2018 changed some of these rules and sends readers to the legislature's site for details.

sections.h2: How much is Michigan transfer tax on an Isabella County sale?
sections.html:
Michigan taxes the transfer of real estate at the state level under Act 330 of 1993 and at the county level under Act 134 of 1966. Ask the Register of Deeds for the dollar amount at your sale price, and expect your title company to print it on the settlement statement.

A few statutory exemptions come up with house transfers, and both acts require the claim to appear on the deed:

  • A conveyance that creates or ends a tenancy by the entireties between spouses.
  • A deed used to straighten a boundary line when no money changes hands.
  • An instrument that confirms a title already vested, such as a quitclaim that fixes a flaw.
  • A joint tenancy created among people when at least one already owns the property.

Transfers to a child or grandchild appear only in the state act, which matters if you plan to gift a house to family.

sections.h2: Does a university town change how a house sale works?
sections.html:
Paperwork is identical, yet the buyer pool differs. Central Michigan University sits in the county, and the 2020 census recorded a median age of 31.7, far below the other three counties in this set. Only 61.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied in the 2020 to 2024 QuickFacts figures, the lowest share among the four, and renters occupied 39.9 percent of occupied units in 2020.

For a landlord selling a rental near campus, that means a deed from an investor-owned property that may have tenants in place. Read any lease before you fix a closing date. Part of Mount Pleasant also lies within the Isabella Indian Reservation, which spans 217.67 square miles and is the main land base of the Saginaw Chippewa Tribal Nation. Ask your title company whether your parcel sits inside the reservation and what that means for the paperwork.

sections.h2: What do Isabella County housing numbers look like?
sections.html:
The July 2025 estimate is 64,691 residents, half a percent above April 2020. Typical home value among owners is $170,400, typical rent is $913, and typical household income is $55,237. Poverty touches 19.0 percent of residents. Adults with a bachelor's degree make up 31.3 percent, the best showing of the four counties, and workers travel 19.6 minutes on average.

The county issued 90 building permits in 2025. Just 78.5 percent of residents had stayed put for a full year, a lower share than in the other three counties in this set.

sections.h2: How is the next tax bill affected after an Isabella County sale?
sections.html:
Selling resets taxable value, according to Michigan Treasury: under Proposal A the cap lifts in the calendar year following the transfer. Form 2766, the Property Transfer Affidavit, is the paper the new owner sends to the local assessor. Section 211.27a(7) of the General Property Tax Act lists transfers that do not uncap.

Tax assessment in Michigan is mostly a city and township task, not a county one. Contact the assessor for the city or township where the house sits about its taxable value and the filing deadline.

faqs.q: How much does a deed cost to file in Isabella County?
faqs.a: $30.00 flat per document, plus $3.00 for each additional liber and page listed beyond the one included at no charge. A tax certificate, when required, costs $5.00 for up to five descriptions.

faqs.q: Who issues the tax certificate for an Isabella County warranty deed?
faqs.a: The county treasurer's office. Your check for the certificate is payable to the Treasurer, and it must be obtained before the Register of Deeds records a warranty deed, land contract or condominium master deed.

faqs.q: How do I get my filed deed returned by mail?
faqs.a: Send a self-addressed stamped envelope with the document. The office asks for one so it can mail the recorded paper back.

faqs.q: Will Isabella County staff review my deed for legal problems?
faqs.a: No. The office does not prepare documents or answer legal questions, and it recommends reviewing every document against the recording requirements before submitting it. Use an attorney for legal help.

faqs.q: What does a name search cost at the Isabella County office?
faqs.a: Fifty cents for every year searched, set by MCL 600.2567, with a $5.00 floor. Copies pulled from a search are billed at the statutory copy rate.
